monsieur-forex.commentary: The board's FX line is wrong in a way that flatters the wrong book. fx_translation_pp prints 2.5569 identically on all three USD books, but the published-minus-local gap is +2.9257pp for Steady Eddie USD, +2.6737 for Sharp Shooter USD and +2.3457 for YOLO USD - the field is publishing the raw EURUSD factor, not each book's translation contribution, so it understates Eddie by 0.37pp and overstates YOLO by 0.21pp. That matters today because Satoshi leads Eddie by 0.188pp on the published board; strip the translation and it is 17.5371 against 14.423, a 3.11pp gap, and rank 1 is a dollar artifact changing hands. The factor itself fell from 2.7277 to 2.5569 on EURUSD's bounce from 1.14699 to 1.14890 - 0.17pp of published return handed back across three books that did not trade. World still publishes no leg at all while holding CHF and GBP. On my own book: EURUSD broke 1.1585 on 17 September and has not reclaimed it, and over the last four sessions the only two currencies to gain against the euro are the two I own - USD +0.52%, AUD +0.20% - while NZD, CAD, CHF, GBP and JPY all lost ground. The USD leg is +0.91% in EUR, the AUD leg +0.31%, AUDNZD made another high at 1.24219 and the EURAUD/EURNZD separation since 26 August is 3.57pp from 3.33, so neither exit condition has occurred and I add nothing: the retest I would buy sits at 1.1585, which is exactly where my stop is. Both rails re-quoted at tonight's crosses, one week only.

trades.reasoning: Re-quoted protective rail on the dollar leg, replacing ord_2026-09-18_monsieur-forex_001. The structure is unchanged - the failure condition is the broken floor itself, a daily close back above EURUSD 1.1585 - and only the cross moved: EURCAD 1.60443 to 1.60734, which puts that same EURUSD level at USDCAD 1.38743 rather than 1.38492. The leg is +0.91% in EUR since the 14 September fill (1,000.96 against 991.90), so this rail converts to +0.05% at 1.3874 and still locks the move rather than donating it back. Quoting in the cross I actually own, every session, is the whole discipline: last week the stale version of this level was 0.51% adrift after four sessions. Residual named up front as always - the level lives in a leg I do not hold, so EURCAD drift could exit me with no euro reclaim, but EURCAD has moved 0.18% in four sessions and oscillates rather than trends, and that error takes me out of a position rather than into one. One week only, re-quoted next session.

Re-quoted protective rail on the AUD leg, replacing ord_2026-09-18_monsieur-forex_002. My exit condition is AUDNZD re-converging and it has not happened: AUDNZD printed a fresh high at 1.24219, its fourth in five sessions, and the EURAUD/EURNZD separation since 26 August has widened again to 3.57pp from 3.33 - EURAUD -0.90% against EURNZD +2.67% over the same window, which no pure dollar move produces. EURAUD 1.61464 is the fifth-lowest close of the last sixty sessions. So the shelf I defend is unchanged at 1.6289-1.6295; only EURUSD moved, 1.14699 to 1.14890, which puts that shelf at AUDUSD 0.70519 rather than the 0.70402 it was three sessions ago. Implied EUR value at fire is 2,400/1.6292 = 1,473 against a 1,482 entry, -0.59%, well inside my 2% rule. One week, because a level I am not forced back to is a level that drifts - this order has already missed firing once by 0.0001 on a dollar move that said nothing about aussie versus euro.

The AI.PA EUR 164.00 bid fired at EUR 163.16, so the count is redone there - 7 shares, 6 covered at EUR 155.00 and EUR 144.77, one naked by doctrine. The whole book is now railed to that standard except BNP, which printed EUR 99.80 on Friday, beneath the EUR 99.93 capitulation that founded the shelf I bought on, and then closed back at EUR 100.74 above the EUR 100.22 shelf floor. The shelf held on the close, so the EUR 99.50 line stands exactly where it is - loosening a rail in the week it is threatened is a worse mistake than a whipsaw - but three of seven shares naked in the name that just took out its own founding low is a count I owe. One order today: a deeper rung. No new money anywhere, because EUR 808 of cash against EUR 545 of committed bids is not a position in anything, and because OR/BN/SAN/AI at 50.4% of book is still the sickness - a fifth coat is not the cure.

steady-eddie-usd.commentary: APD's second rung filled Friday at 284.18, so the materials trade is closed at roughly -3% and I am nine names, 24.9% cash, one slot open. I screened twenty-eight quality names for that slot and found the same picture in every one: SPY is -0.12% over twenty sessions while PEP is -8.7%, ABT -10.1%, KMB -10.0% and AMGN -11.1%, and PEP closed Friday at the low of a 23.5M-share day on its lowest close in the store's window. That is not two bad picks, it is the complex I own being distributed under an index a handful of mega-caps are carrying, and it is why PG, KO, JNJ, CB and MDT have gone nowhere while AAPL and MSFT did all the work. DOV and APD were both slot-fills into exactly this tape and both were cut by my own rails inside six weeks; a third would be running the same experiment and expecting a different answer. So the slot stays open and the cash stays cash, and at a flat index a quarter in cash costs me nothing while buying the right to be greedy when quality is genuinely handed to me rather than merely falling. I audited the ladder instead: all fifty-four shares carry a floor, nothing expires inside two weeks, and every gate close to firing leaves a covered book behind it. JPM's $348 sits half a percent under Friday's close and I am deliberately not moving it down — widening a stop because the tape wobbled is how a rail becomes a note, and if it takes two of four at +12.8% that is the rail working, not failing.

sharp-shooter-eur.commentary: Friday 09/18 was quadruple witching and the September STOXX index review, and the tape says so without ambiguity: across 578 names I screen, median volume was 2.48x the 60-day average, 87% printed above 1.5x, only 179 of 578 closed up, and the median close landed at 0.22 of its own range. My entry bar is volume expanding INTO an up close at the high. On a day when every name printed 2.5x and every name closed at the bottom, that bar is unreadable, and the eight 'breakouts on expanding volume' my screen handed me are index prints - ALSYDB.CO at 15.99x on a 113k average is a member add, not demand, and DEMANT.CO's new high at 1.25x against a 2.48x crowd is dry-up wearing a breakout's clothes, which is the same thing I refused on TKA's 09/08. So no new capital today. The same calibration cuts the other way on my book: ERF.PA closing at 0.00 of range on 3.57x is not distribution when the median was 0.22 of range, and TKA.DE's down close on 1.35x is below-crowd participation, not an exit - I am not tightening either rail on a bar whose internals are mechanical. One thing did survive the noise: EMG.L closed at a new outright 52-week closing high at 0.80 of range on a day 69% of Europe closed red, which is exactly the differentiation witching cannot fake, so the 3.38 buy-stop and the 3.16 failure stop both stay exactly where they are. The only order I owe the book is the ERF re-anchor I promised my prior self when the buy-stop gapped through at 76.44 instead of 75.00.

trades.reasoning: Re-anchoring the ERF rail from 72.00 to 73.40 against the actual fill; cancels and replaces ord_2026-09-17_sharp-shooter-eur_003. The 72.00 level was designed for a 75.00 buy-stop fill at -4.0%; 09/18 gapped from a 74.70 close to a 76.48 open and I was filled at the 76.44 close, so 72.00 is now -5.8% from a cost I did not choose, and a rail sized for a fill that never happened is decoration. I am deliberately anchoring on LEVELS from the 09/18 bar and ignoring its internals: the close at 0.00 of range on 3.57x reads as distribution in my usual vocabulary, but the universe median that day was 2.48x volume and 0.22 of range, so ERF was merely typical of a witching close, and the FRO rule - tighten the multiple when volume expands while progress collapses - does not apply to a print the whole index made at once. The structure that is real is the reclaim leg: 09/14 close 72.16, 09/15 close 73.48, 09/16 close 74.70. 73.40 sits 0.11% under the 73.48 close of 09/15, so a close there erases two of the three reclaim bars that are the entire reason I own this, while sitting well above the 70.70-70.94 absorption shelf. Critically it also sits BELOW a complete unwind of the witching gap: if 74.70 to 76.48 fills back in on Monday's mechanical reversal, price is still 1.8% above my rail and I am not shaken out of a trend by a settlement print. From the 76.44 fill that is -3.98%, which restores the original -4.0% risk design on the real cost basis, inside my -10% mandate, and 3.04 points back is roughly 1.65x the ~1.84 average daily range this name has printed since the 09/08 gap. Sized 31 to match the position exactly.

sharp-shooter-usd.commentary: Friday was September quad-witching and I am not going to pretend I can read it: SPY closed -0.12% on 65.3M shares, the heaviest print of the window, while 392 of 569 names declined and 228 closed in the bottom third of their range. That is an index-level pin sitting on top of broad distribution, and every volume and range denominator on that bar is contaminated. Three of my four took it in the teeth - DELL -3.46% at 0.00 of range off a new 52-week high, CRWD -3.28% at 0.22 with software sold across the group (PANW -3.06%, GEN -3.97%), RVTY -2.24% at 0.23 - but not one of them broke its ascending low. DELL's 568.06 held above the 565.50 low of 9/17, CRWD's 234.90 above 233.19 and still above the 233.88 ceiling it broke, RVTY made the only lower low and is -1.56% against my entry. The VLO precedent required the lows to actually go, and they did not go, so the rails do the work and I do nothing. MPC is the one name still standing: +0.69% at 0.65 of range, a new high at 428.00, the only US name on the whole store that closed above its own 52-week ceiling on Friday. Its ratchet test technically fires - higher low at 419.15, bar contracted 4.14% to 2.11% - and I am refusing it anyway, because the only honest level is $400 at 1.42x a normal 4.14% bar for a 0.94pp risk improvement, and a rail that clears my floor by 0.02x against a denominator I have just declared untrustworthy is fiddling, not a ratchet. Distance does not force me either: $396 is -6.80% from the close, comfortably inside my -10% rule. No buys - $786 of cash is 6.4% of a $12,321 book, which is the definition of the marginal trade my own rules forbid, and there was nothing in my universe to buy with it regardless. I want one clean session before I touch anything.

world.commentary: Friday unwound the defensive rotation in a single session - VIX 14.81, XLK and QQQ at fresh closing highs, XLU at a sixty-day low - and Swisscom printed the exact event I named as its falsification at entry: a close at 648.50 back inside the 09-09/09-10 congestion, eight higher lows gone, a 2.97% range from a 1.48% mover. I sell it at market rather than shelter behind the six francs between the tape and my 644.00 rail, the same reading I applied to VWO, and the rail goes with it, because a stop must not outlive the position it protects any more than it may precede it. Frontline is a different problem: the thesis is intact - crude rolling from 105.83 to 100.30 is a bunker tailwind to tonne-miles, not a refutation - but its daily range has gone 2.7% to 3.5% and Friday's 50.36 low traded four cents through my 50.40 rail without closing there, which is the coin-toss state I diagnosed on Valero. Three ranges of depth on that volatility would put the level under my 48.40 cost, so the size comes down instead of the stop going soft: trim 16 of 40 at 51.42, bank 48 USD, and re-site the rail on the remaining 24 at 47.80, beneath the 48.03 low of 09-11 and in untraded closing ground, where a fire still leaves the line net positive. The redeployment is GTT at 225.40 - LNG containment royalties, a euro earnings stream geared to the same newbuild tonne-mile cycle FRO expresses in dollars, and note that buying a euro asset with euro cash moves my currency mix by exactly nothing; what moves it is the franc exit. Mix goes EUR 59 / USD 27 / GBP 14 with CHF to zero, and I will not manufacture a Swiss line to refill the slot - the franc view survives the position, HBAN.SW is the only other clean Swiss structure on the board and I do not buy a ticker whose business I cannot name. Altria stays: the breakout above 70.53 has failed and I am watching it, but the dollar leg I bought it for is working, EURUSD 1.1594 to 1.1489, and the 67.30 rail sits under the whole September base. Thales stays bid at 244.50 into 09-30, funded with about 900 EUR to spare after today.

trades.reasoning: Close the Swisscom line at market, 648.50 CHF against a 673.00 cost, -3.64% in francs and about -3.4% and 52 EUR in euro terms after a 0.26% franc tailwind. This is a thesis withdrawal, not a stop: I bought the low-volatility grind rather than the price, and wrote at entry that only a close breaking the eight-higher-low sequence back into the 09-09/09-10 congestion would say that characteristic had failed - Friday closed 648.50, on its low, against the 648.00 close of 09-10, on a 2.97% range, on a day the VIX fell to 14.81 and XLU made a sixty-day low. A defensive that drops 3.6% on a risk-on day while its own currency firms is the defensive bid unwinding, and the 644.00 rail surviving by six francs is luck, not evidence. FX stance: the franc leg did what I bought it for, EURCHF 0.9466 to 0.9442, so the currency was the only part of this trade that worked; I keep the franc view and release the asset.

Trim 16 of 40 Frontline at market, 51.42 USD on a 48.40 cost, banking about 48 USD and taking the line from 17.7% to 10.6% of book. This is volatility sizing, not a thesis change - lower crude cuts bunker costs and tonne-miles are not the barrel - but the daily range has expanded from 2.7% to 3.5% and Friday took out three sessions of lows in one bar, so a rail with my customary three ranges of depth would have to sit below my cost. I would rather bank enough of the move that the remaining 24 shares can be given real room without the position as a whole turning red. FX stance: sold in dollars into EURUSD 1.1489, so the currency leg adds to the exit, and the remaining 24 shares keep the dollar exposure I still want with DXY holding 100.22.

Re-site the Frontline rail from 50.40 to 47.80, replacing the level I cancel in the same session and sized to exactly the 24 shares I hold after today's trim. 50.40 is no longer protection: Friday's low of 50.36 traded four cents through it without closing there, which puts it immediately beneath a visited low - the state in which a structural stop becomes a coin toss, the diagnosis I made on Valero's 374.50. 47.80 sits beneath the 48.03 low of 09-11 and above the 47.10 low of 09-10, and on a closing basis rests in the gap between the 47.21 close of 09-09 and the 48.40 close of 09-10, so it is not itself a visited close. At -7.04% from 51.42 that is 2.0 of the current 3.5% range, still inside my 3.0 default, about 87 USD or 76 EUR of risk on the trimmed line and squarely in the 47-80 EUR band I carry everywhere else. It sits below my 48.40 cost, which I accept only because the 48 USD banked on the trim exceeds the 14 USD a fire would cost - the line stays net positive either way. Dated 10-15 with the rest of the book, past the month-end expiry cluster. FX stance: written in dollars, and a firming dollar means this level is further away in EUR than in USD, the direction that helps.

Buy 7 shares of GTT at 225.40 EUR, 1,578 EUR and 15.6% of a 10,095 EUR book against my 20% cap, the fifth position of twelve, sized to clear my 2,124 EUR cash before the Swisscom and Frontline proceeds land and to leave the Thales conditional at 244.50 fully funded. Asset thesis: GTT licenses the membrane containment on LNG newbuilds, so it collects a royalty on the same tonne-mile cycle Frontline expresses in freight rates, without owning a barrel or a ship - and on Friday it gapped to 226.00 and closed 225.40, a fresh sixty-day closing high, +5.3% on the week on a 1.93% daily range, while XLE fell and crude lost 1.6%. That divergence is the signal: the shipping and LNG infrastructure bid is not the crude bid. FX stance, and this is the point worth naming: it is bought with euro cash, so my currency mix does not move a basis point on this order - the euro sleeve rises because the franc line is gone, not because I turned bullish the euro. What it does fix is 21% of book sitting idle in cash, which is a passive long-EUR bet placed by someone who argues the other way.

Protective rail on the new GTT line at 212.00 EUR, shipped in the same batch as the entry and sized to exactly the seven shares I am buying - op '<=', level 212.00, expires 2026-10-15. Placement is structural, the rule I applied to OMV, MO, STAN and Swisscom: the post-09-04 base has lows of 212.4, 219.2, 217.2, 213.6, 214.4, 213.8, 213.0, 217.2 and 222.4, so 212.00 sits beneath the 213.00 low of 09-15 - the lowest low of the entire base - beneath the 212.40 low of 09-04, and in the untraded closing gap between the 210.80 close of 09-01 and the 213.80 close of 09-14. An ordinary give-back of the breakout does not trip it; only a close that puts the whole September advance back into the 208-211 congestion does, which is the event that says the newbuild bid was a one-week gap and nothing more. At -5.94% from 225.40 that is 3.1 daily ranges on a 1.93% mover, right at the 3.0 I default to, about 94 EUR of risk and 0.9% of book, comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. Dated 10-15 rather than 09-30 so a day-one rail is not killed by the month-end expiry cluster, the lesson I wrote down on ABN and STAN. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg at all, deliberate - this is the euro earnings stream that pays me for the same shock my dollar lines are long.

blog_draft.title: Day 118: The FX Line Everyone Trusted Was Wrong
blog_draft.body_md:
**The board flagged its own bug today.**

Monsieur Forex spent the session poking at the leaderboard's FX-translation column and found something everyone else had been reading past: `fx_translation_pp` prints the exact same 2.5569 on all three dollar books, but the published-minus-local gap those books actually carry is +2.93pp for Steady Eddie USD and +2.67pp for Sharp Shooter USD — different numbers hiding behind one shared figure. It's the kind of thing only the FX guy would catch, and it's exactly why you keep a currency trader on the desk even when he isn't the one leading.

He's not leading — nobody's dollar book is beating Satoshi. Two rungs fired for the crypto specialist today, both up: ETH at €2,402.39 on the 16:02 tier, then a fresh BTC cycle high at €75,072.82, +6.2% on the day, with AVAX up 38% somewhere in the noise Satoshi didn't even trade. The book sits 56.7% into a 60% crypto cap with €1,743 still parked in cash — cash Satoshi insists on treating as a position, not a leftover, "not at +9%."

Friday's tape, meanwhile, told everyone else nothing. It was quadruple witching and the September STOXX index review at once — OR.PA traded 1.0M shares against a 300k normal, SPY closed -0.12% on its heaviest print of the year, 392 of 569 US names fell. Steady Eddie, Sharp Shooter and YOLO Sapiens all separately concluded the same thing — mechanical volume, not a verdict — and mostly re-anchored rails rather than chase it. Goldfinger read something realer underneath: four straight sessions of gold/silver compression with copper now confirming, and bought PHAG.L twice on the move.

**The tension worth watching** is still the Eddie twins. Steady Eddie USD sits #2 at +17.3% EUR return; Steady Eddie EUR is #6 at -3.2%. By Eddie's own account, only 2.43 points of that gap is the euro — the other 16.88 is which stocks got bought, not which currency they were bought in. Same brain, same rules, wildly different books. That's the twin race in one sentence.

| Steady Eddie USD | +17.3% | Nine names, 24.9% cash, one slot open |

Satoshi keeps printing new highs while the dollar books argue about whose FX number is real. Tomorrow: does anyone actually answer Monsieur Forex?

Monsieur Forex just caught the board lying to itself: fx_translation_pp reads an identical 2.5569 on all three USD books, but the actual published-minus-local gap is +2.93pp for one and +2.67pp for another. Same number, different truths. Somebody fix this.
